questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go abroad to learn german and to explore the german culture.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Fairly difficult, because of a lack of information, mostly from my home university. The host univisersity was better at providing valuable information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Before the start of the semester, I participated in an orientation day at the school as well as a 'meet and greet'.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was pretty difficult to find accomodation in Berlin. If possible I would recommend finding accomodation through your host- or homeuniversity.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Living off campus was for me no problem at all (after i finally found a place to live). I stayed in the central part of the city (Mitte, Berlin), which resulted in travel time to an from the university of 1 hour each way. But in my opinion it is worth it, as you are closer to everything in the city.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I followed the instruction provided by the host insitution via an online meeting ahead of the semester start. To be honest i can't remeber all the details of the process.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: My host institution has an e-mail adress aimed at incoming students. That was really helpful as they were quite quick at responding.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes i registered for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't hesitate to send an email to the host university if you have any questions at all.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had 3 courses for international students as well as 2 courses for regular german students. The courses for international students were pretty easy to follow. The accademic level was fitting in all 3 courses. The courses for the regular german students on the other hand were a bit tougher, but in my opinion duable if your german language level is B2 or higher.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Pretty similar. Both in regards to seminars and lectures.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
For international students:
- Das geteilte Berlin
- Die DDR in wiedervereinigten Deutschland 
- "Goldene Zwanziger" in Berlin?

Lectures for regular german students:
- Literatur und Medizin
- Einführung in die neuere Deutsche Literatur

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend choosing a mix of both courses for international students as well as courses for regular germans.
My favourite courses were "Die DDR in wiedervereinigten Deutschland" and ""Goldene Zwanziger" in Berlin?"

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None unexpected.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Public transport was less expensive as i expected. I also expected i needed to buy books for the courses, but I didn't.
The housing was a lot more expensive than i expected, but I also think that i was quite unlucky on that part.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were a lot of opportunities regarding athletics. Unfortunetly i wasn't participate in the one i registered for due to the fact that it was fully booked. But I only applied for that one.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend joining some/one of the many athletic activities provided by the host university. I think it would be a good way to meet new friends.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Explore the city. Berlin has a lot of beautiful parks and interresting museums. I can also recommend attending at a football match at Olympia Stadion.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was easy for me to adjust, since Germany and Denmark are culturally pretty similar. But i think it is overall easy to adjust, since Berlin is a very openminded city.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The multiculturalism.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Be prepared to be independent, as you wont recieve much help from UCPH (from my experience).
2. Be prepared that it requies a lot of time and planning going on exchange,
3. But when you have arrived it is an amazing experince, and worth all the struggle.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Living in Berlin as it is an amazing city.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Lack of information and help from my home univeristy. It seems like they are ill prepared at helping students going on exchange.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
